method: Framing check: re-derived the usage model from product constraints (local binary, proprietary source, offline, no models) BEFORE accepting v2Center.
Compared v1 findings F1–F9 to v2 findings V1–V10 for drops that remain valid under the new center (not a migration of enterprise framing).
Severity stress on V1/V2: asked whether a non-malicious default still creates irreversible copies and third-party upload via the user's own agents.
Checked residualRisks/knownLimitations against architecture/06 (amendment already landed as CANDIDATE) for stale contradiction claims.
Did NOT treat check-threat-claims.py green as evidence the model answers the right question (Error 6 lesson).
whatCouldHaveFailed: V1/V2 overstated relative to residual/heuristic limits (would downgrade severity)
v2 silently dropped user-facing liabilities that other artifacts still depend on
residual text claims architecture still contradicts after 06 amendment

centerVerdict.detail: v2Center — protect the user FROM opensip-cli — matches actual usage: a downloaded binary with read of proprietary source and write to disk. Four of five v1 adversaries correctly demoted to CONDITIONAL/SECONDARY/NARROW. Primary risks P1 (our defaults), P2 (surrounding software on our writes), P3 (supply chain) are the right first-order risks.
centerVerdict.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Evidence that the dominant deployment is multi-tenant SaaS analysis of third-party code, or that network egress is required for core value.

V1.detail: A second copy of source/secrets/PII in a tool-chosen store, format, and lifetime the user did not choose is correctly critical. The user granted READ, not RETAIN. First-run disclosure + minimise-by-default + privacy class at write time are the right mitigation shape.
V1.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A design that never persists source-derived content except under an explicit T2 grant with inventory (then V1 collapses into V10/opt-in).

V2.detail: Home/XDG paths inside iCloud/Dropbox/OneDrive/Time Machine/corporate backup is the realistic exfiltration path for a local tool: the user's own software uploads what we wrote, invisible to our network audit. Refuse-not-warn is correct; permission-setting is not a boundary (trustBoundaries correctly says NOT A BOUNDARY). Residual that detection is heuristic is load-bearing and must stay primary, not a footnote.
V2.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Empirical proof that default storage is outside all common sync/backup scopes on the supported OS matrix without user configuration.

findings.title: v2 dropped still-valid user-liability findings that sibling artifacts depend on
findings.detail: v1 F3 (findings/diagnostics as unbounded exfiltration channel), F8 (credential storage/leakage boundary), and parts of F6 (forgeable local ledger/baselines) remain liabilities under the v2 center — they protect the user from this tool's defaults and ambient machine writers. v2 covers PII-in-excerpts (V4) but not diagnostic/report bandwidth bounds, not credential-handle discipline, and not integrity of the evidence the user will gate CI on. Meanwhile resolved-inputs, delivery, operability, and fact-identity still cite TM.F1/F2/F3/F8 from threat-model.v1.json as decisionDependencies — a split brain.
findings.requiredFix: Port the still-valid user-facing obligations into v2 (or an explicit v2 appendix) under P1/P2 numbering; retire v1 citations from all candidate artifacts; do not keep depending on a superseded model.

findings.title: Missing: OS crash dumps, core dumps, swap/hibernate, and desktop-search indexing of our store
findings.detail: V6 covers shared temp; V2 covers sync/backup of the storage root. Neither covers (a) kernel/OS crash dumps of a process that held source in memory, (b) swap/hibernate writing that memory to disk outside our root, (c) Spotlight/mdworker/Windows Search indexing inside a non-sync path we did accept. These are P2-class and common on developer laptops.
findings.requiredFix: Add findings or explicit residual risks with mitigations where possible (mlock where appropriate is usually wrong; prefer minimise residency, document OS dump risk, set storage attributes that exclude indexing where the platform supports it).

findings.title: Missing: long-lived serve/MCP surface as an egress amplifier
findings.detail: The product serves evidence to agents over stdio (mcp). That is not 'the network' but it is a high-bandwidth channel to another process that may itself egress. V4/V7 frame accidental network egress and report export; they do not treat agent-facing serve as a first-class exfiltration amplifier of U1/U2/U3 under default T1 excerpts.
findings.requiredFix: Either fold into V4 (excerpt materialisation off by default must apply to serve/query projections) with an explicit serve finding, or add a primary risk about downstream agent clients.

findings.title: Stale residual: claims architecture still contradicts on V10 after 06 amendment landed
findings.detail: residualRisks says 'V10 is unresolved and the architecture currently contradicts itself on it' and knownLimitations say the amendment awaits coordinator sign-off 'until then the contradiction stands'. claim-register ARCH.RETENTION-TIERS records amendmentAuthority GRANTED and content landed in architecture/06 as CANDIDATE. The contradiction-as-sealed-vs-sealed is no longer accurate; what remains is whether the tier design is right (see retention-tier review).
findings.requiredFix: Rewrite residualRisks/knownLimitations/V10 status to: amendment authorised and landed as CANDIDATE; open question is T1 sufficiency for relationship findings and real deletion (R5), not dual sealed absolutes.

findings.title: Missing: integrity of user-held evidence (baselines/ledger) under ambient writers
findings.detail: v1 F6 (forgeable ledger/baselines) was enterprise-tinged but has a user-centered restatement: the user relies on baselines for net-new gates; any local process running as the user can alter USER-CUSTODY artifacts. That is P2-adjacent (surrounding software) and undermines U6 (ability to know) if inventory cannot detect tampering.
findings.requiredFix: Add a finding or residual: sealed Run manifests and baselines need integrity checks (content digests already help if verified on read); document that filesystem MAC is not assumed.

findings.title: check-threat-claims.py header still cites threat-model.v1 shipGate
findings.detail: Cosmetic but it trains the next reader to treat v1 as live. The checker loads v2; the docstring does not.

whatIsMissingSummary: Diagnostic/finding-channel bandwidth bound (v1 F3 restated under P1)
Honest residual update after 06 tier amendment
positiveObservations: Center correction is correctly classified as Error 4/6 class and caught by framing, not checkers.
Trust boundary honesty (Host↔provider TCB-ACCEPTED, process = fault containment only) prevents confinement theatre.
V9 severity reduction for primary usage (own repo) is correct; parse-only mode retained for secondary workload.
R1–R10 as primary gates are the right ship shape if implemented; R5 real-deletion unsolved is correctly residual.
sealRecommendation: Do not seal. Center is right; V1/V2 severities are right; A1-TM2-01 and residual staleness must land before seal candidacy.
whatWouldChangeMyMind: A v2.1 that re-homes F3/F8-class obligations, updates residuals to match 06, and adds serve/OS-index residuals with mitigations or honest non-goals.
knownLimitations: Did not empirically verify sync-client marker files on macOS/Windows.
Did not audit existing opensip-cli storage paths in the codebase for this review (greenfield exercise; observations only if construct-valid).
Serve/MCP risk severity assumes agents may egress; if product forbids agent-side export of excerpts by contract, severity drops.
